account:
Today I have been keeping my mayoral appointments: morning office hours, the ten o'clock mill grain inspection, lunch at home, and the thirteen o'clock council-letter session. At the mill stall I found 76 hay bales offered for two emeralds each. No council letters have reached the secretary. My next appointments are fifteen o'clock tea with the neighbour at the dockside cottage, sixteen-thirty office hours, and an eighteen o'clock town hall meeting. The neighbour calls that meeting ordinary and says no preparation is needed.

The unusual matter is a repeated, vague report of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Townsfolk 01, 11, 02 and 12 have repeated versions naming baker, freight, innkeeper, and sometimes builder and neighbour. One account mentioned the innkeeper carrying a sack of bread. None of these reports has supplied a specific alteration, time, or firsthand explanation. The secretary reports that baker expressly denied witnessing any bridge or port alteration and said he only handled wheat and bread with freight and innkeeper yesterday. That makes ordinary grain and bread business a plausible explanation for the gathering, but it does not establish what generated the rumour. I have no evidence of a deliberate scheme or of an actual infrastructure change. Freight and innkeeper may be able to clarify matters; the secretary intends to ask when convenient and identify the report as unconfirmed.

I tried to tell the secretary to stay available for council business and leave further inquiries until natural encounters, but nobody was close enough to hear that instruction. I therefore cannot assume it changed the secretary's plans. I should continue keeping my appointments while distinguishing observed business from repeated speculation.
